headline: Approved previous meeting minutes; discussed mattress recycling, clothing swaps, and composting proposal.
summary: Members discussed mattress recycling and curbside mattress costs, clothing swaps, and a composting proposal to the Mayor's Office. The only vote recorded was to approve the previous meeting minutes, which passed unanimously.
decisions: Approved the previous meeting minutes by unanimous vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Chairperson Alice Kosowsky introduced a motion to approve the previous meeting minutes, and was seconded by Commissioner Theresa Allgood. The motion passed by unanimous vote.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Solid Waste & Recycling Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, September 9, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER   
 
• Chairperson Alice Kosowky called the meeting to order at 7:04 PM.  
 
2. ATTENDANCE   
 
• Present: Commissioners Shenira Billups, Eben Pariser, and Theresa Allgood, Alice 
Kosowsky (Chair), and Joe DeRisi, Recycling coordinator.  
 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 
•  Chairperson Alice Kosowsky introduced a motion to approve the previous meeting 
minutes, and was seconded by Commissioner Theresa Allgood. The motion passed 
by unanimous vote. 
 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 
• No public comment 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE   
 
• No correspondence 
 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 
• No need for Executive Session  
 
7. REPORTS   
 
• Another clothing swap coming up on the 26th?
• Brooksvale Park Swap, part of the Fall Fest will take place at 11 AM-4 PM on 
September 26. Best Video will also have a clothing swap on the same day at 10 
AM-12 PM, and the leftover clothes from Best Video will be brought to the 
Brooksvale Park event. 
• Upcoming meeting with Public Works 
 
8. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  1. Swaps  
  
• Staffing and scheduling for the first clothing swap taking place in the southern 
part of town, this Thursday, Sept 10, 2026.  
 
  2. Proposal to the Mayor's Office.  
  
• A proposal and proof of concept on food waste, yard and leaf composting at 
the transfer station is to be submitted to the Mayor's Office. 
 
  3. Public Education Campaign  
  
• Education campaign to inform and inspire people to action. 
• Five points to be presented in a series of infographics and posters, along with 
a podcast on each of the five points 
 
9. NEW BUSINESS   
 
• A DPR and tire collection plan would translate into a $30K/year saving.  
• Addressing the glitch at the transfer station as it relates to mattresses (In 2022, we 
recycled 75% of mattresses that came into the transfer station. However, in 2025, 
we only recycled 17% of what came in) 
• Responding to the challenge of curbside mattresses. (In 2022, 1200 mattresses 
were placed curbside. In 2025, it was 1208, and it costs $33.50 to throw one out). 
Not throwing out the bulk of mattresses left at curbside would represent another 
potential $36K in savings. 
• A potential mattress recovery program could save the town an additional $36K-
$40K and could save around 30 tons from our waste stream. 
• Composting is a future Commission priority. We should embrace it 
• Joe will present a proposal to the Mayor exploring two paths: Domingo’s peels and 
wheels public private partnership (PPP) loan to build a capacious in-vessel 
container at transfer stations, or Eben’s revenue-neutral idea as long as water, pad, 
and electricity are provided.
• Textile: Textile is being addressed with three swaps. The current swaps aren't as 
high as the previous ones, but they still fall within the top 4 months (3500–4000 
pounds of textile). 
• The need to fix the roof at the barn to allow it to serve as a semi-permanent clothing 
swap space. 
• Bulk pick up: Much more complicated, but there is potential to explore ideas such as 
the Mansfield reconstruction Center. Other towns have a shop where you can bring 
furniture in a swapping program. A swap shop is a great idea, but would require 
management.  
 
10. ADJOURNMENT   
 
• Chairperson Alice Kosowsky motioned to adjourn the meeting at 8:15PM. 
• Commissioner Eben Pariser seconded the motion.    
• The motion was approved by unanimous vote.
